clue.text: Where American bigwigs may come together for sex?

definitions.text: Where American bigwigs may come together
definitions.meaning: the US legislature, where senators and representatives assemble
an old formal word for sexual intercourse is the same word as the legislature's name

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about what powerful Americans get up to when they meet.
explanation.definitionFit: The US national legislature bears this name, and the same word is a dated, formal term for sexual union.

clue.text: Right-wing party requiring mass protection

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the British right-wing party
a do is a party
m is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A conservative political group needs broad public support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right-wing party' looks like one unit and 'mass' like popular support, but each is a separate short piece.
explanation.definitionFit: This sheath is a form of protection against pregnancy and infection.

clue.text: Provider of daily information given to Secret Service operative

indicators.note: given to means added next to, so the operative follows

parts.note: news is information supplied daily
an agent is an operative of the Secret Service

explanation.surface: Someone passes the daily briefing to a presidential bodyguard.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling papers supplies, or provides, the daily papers to customers.

clue.text: Competed as a candidate prior to winning and accumulated debts?

indicators.note: prior to means coming before, so the first piece comes first

parts.note: a candidate who stood for office ran
a team that is winning is up

explanation.surface: A candidate who ran and won ended up in debt from campaigning.
explanation.definitionFit: To run up a bill is to accumulate charges, so one ran up debts; the question mark flags the phrasal sense.

clue.text: Rice possibly is upset with the heads of Dubya's executive organisation

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word is upside down, so it reads from the bottom
the heads of the words are their first letters

parts.note: order means arrangement or organisation

explanation.surface: Condoleezza Rice is unsettled by the leadership of George W Bush's administration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rice' looks like Condoleezza Rice, Bush's Secretary of State; 'possibly' marks rice as an example of a side order. Dubya is George W Bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Rice is often ordered as an accompaniment to a main dish in a restaurant.

clue.text: After short amount of time, Cruz perhaps becomes very wealthy

indicators.note: the senator's name is placed after the shortened time unit, so it comes second
short means the word for this unit of time is cut down to its usual abbreviation

parts.note: a minute is a small amount of time
Ted Cruz is a US senator; 'perhaps' marks him as one example of a Ted

explanation.surface: A US senator suddenly gets rich almost overnight.
explanation.definitionFit: Being minted is British slang for having plenty of money, as if one could print it.

clue.text: Have a burning desire to throw Pence out

indicators.note: out means the abbreviation for pence is removed

parts.note: to pitch is to throw

explanation.surface: Someone longs to eject Vice President Mike Pence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pence' looks like Mike Pence, but it is the British money unit, abbreviated P.
explanation.definitionFit: To be itching to do something is to have an urgent longing, like a burning wish.

clue.text: Opponent loses heart following tense event in the Supreme Court?

indicators.note: the shortened opponent follows the abbreviation for tense

parts.note: t is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: losing the heart means the middle letter is dropped

parts.note: a rival is an opponent

explanation.surface: A political opponent loses courage after a nerve-racking appearance before the top judges.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the US Supreme Court mostly hears appeals rather than trials.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearing of a case before judges is a trial, the kind of event held in a court.

clue.text: Democrat dealing with vital representation of party?

parts.note: on means about or dealing with
key means vital, essential

explanation.surface: A Democrat handles the key symbolism of their party.
explanation.definitionFit: The donkey is the symbol, or emblem, of the US Democratic Party.

clue.text: A Republican leading each district

explanation.surface: A Republican is ahead in every constituency.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a region or district.

clue.text: Currently elected, and hopeless!

parts.note: currently means at this moment, now
a winning candidate is said to be in

explanation.surface: A cynic's comment on a politician who has just taken office.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-win situation is one where success is impossible, so it is hopeless.

clue.text: Corrupt doctrine overshadows current administration

indicators.note: to overshadow is to cast a cover over, so the rearranged word wraps around the symbol for current
something corrupted is twisted out of shape, so the word doctrine is rearranged

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A complaint that a rotten ideology dominates the present government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' rearranges DOCTRINE into DIRECTON, and 'overshadows' means it wraps round I, entering just before the final ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Direction is management or control, which is what an administration provides.

clue.text: A poor plan — developed with veep's lead — is subject to ratification

indicators.note: a plan that has developed has changed shape, so these letters are rearranged
the lead of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A weak policy, reworked under the vice president's guidance, still needs a formal vote.
explanation.walkthrough: A veep is US slang for a vice president; only its first letter, V, joins A POOR PLAN to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods taken on approval can be returned until the buyer accepts them, so they await confirmation.

clue.text: Politically, the West Coast usually erupted, we're told

indicators.note: something we are told is heard rather than read, so a word sounding the same is wanted

parts.note: a volcano that erupted blew its top

explanation.surface: A political commentator says the West Coast exploded, as reported.
explanation.walkthrough: In US politics blue is the Democratic party's colour, and West Coast states usually vote Democratic.
explanation.definitionFit: States that vote Democratic are coloured blue on American election maps, as the Pacific states typically are.

clue.text: Narcos providing support for one proposal

indicators.note: in a down answer, a support sits beneath, so the narcos go below

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
narcos is US slang for drug agents, the DEA

explanation.surface: Drug dealers back one person's plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Narcos' suggests drug traffickers, but in US slang it also means the narcotics agents of the Drug Enforcement Administration.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a suggestion or plan put forward, a proposal.

clue.text: Block silly vote

indicators.note: something silly is foolish or disordered, so the word vote is rearranged

explanation.surface: A call to stop a foolish ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is the power to stop a law or decision, so to veto is to block it.

clue.text: Bit of hullabaloo at Hoover's inauguration recital

indicators.note: only a bit of the phrase is used, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: A fuss broke out at Herbert Hoover's swearing-in.
explanation.definitionFit: A US president recites a solemn vow of office at the inauguration.

clue.text: Inarticulate aides essentially have lower levels of intelligence

parts.note: dumb in its old sense means unable to speak

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so the middle letter of aides is taken

parts.note: to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: A jibe that tongue-tied political staffers are not very bright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inarticulate aides' reads as a phrase, but 'Inarticulate' is the first piece and only the middle of 'aides' is used.
explanation.definitionFit: To dumb down is to reduce the intellectual content of something so it demands less thought.

clue.text: Policy document is clear and well-founded at heart

parts.note: manifest means clear, obvious

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Praise for a party's programme as transparent and soundly based.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of 'well-founded' (eleven letters, ignoring the hyphen) is O.
explanation.definitionFit: A party publishes its policies before an election in a written statement of aims.

clue.text: A tweet put out with rage almost creates White House scandal

indicators.note: put out suggests disturbed, so the letters are put into disorder
almost means the last letter of rage is cut off

explanation.surface: An angry social media post sparks a presidential scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims RAGE to RAG; 'put out' rearranges A TWEET RAG.
explanation.definitionFit: The Watergate affair was the 1970s scandal that forced Nixon to resign the presidency.

clue.text: Utter ruin leaves one under government control

parts.note: to utter something is to state it

indicators.note: when one leaves, it is taken out of the word ruin

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Complete disaster forces someone into the hands of the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter ruin' reads as total disaster, but 'Utter' is a verb meaning to say.
explanation.definitionFit: A state-run body is operated by the government rather than private owners.

clue.text: Workers from The Hill?

parts.note: The Hill is a nickname for Congress on Capitol Hill, but read literally the workers come from an anthill

explanation.walkthrough: Capitol Hill suggests congressional staff; the hill meant is the mound built by small insects, whose workers are the colony's labourers.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker insects in a colony live in a mound known as a hill, so they are workers from the hill.

clue.text: Uproar in America after 'The Chosen One' loses his head

indicators.note: the American abbreviation goes after the shortened name
losing the head means dropping the first letter

parts.note: Donald Trump once called himself the chosen one
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: Chaos in the US follows a self-proclaimed saviour being toppled.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy disturbance or commotion, an uproar.

clue.text: New taxes irritated the Bushes?

indicators.note: irritated suggests agitated, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: Tax increases annoyed the Bush family.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bush presidential family are from Texas, so the Bushes are examples of residents of that state.

clue.text: Unionist with stovepipe, say, going round western state

indicators.note: to go round is to turn back on itself, so the headwear's letters are read backwards

parts.note: a stovepipe is a tall hat, as worn by Lincoln

explanation.surface: A Union supporter in a tall hat tours the western territories, like a figure from Lincoln's era.
explanation.definitionFit: This mountain state lies in the western United States, between Nevada and Colorado.

clue.text: Foreign article contains 'fake news'?

indicators.note: contains means the article holds the falsehood inside it

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
fake news is a lie

explanation.surface: A news piece from abroad is dismissed as fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien means belonging to another country, foreign.

clue.text: Favoured presidential retreat is grand, and certainly large on the inside

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand dollars

indicators.note: the letter for large is placed inside the phrase meaning certainly

parts.note: of course means certainly
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A wry nod to a president's favourite getaway being both lavish and huge.
explanation.walkthrough: The retreat alludes to a president known for frequent weekends playing at his own resorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Some presidents spend much leisure time on the links, making them a favourite place to relax.

clue.text: Miss Ohio snubbed Senator Romney

parts.note: O is the postal-style abbreviation for Ohio

indicators.note: snubbed suggests snub-nosed, cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Mitt Romney was a US senator for Utah

explanation.surface: A beauty queen from Ohio cold-shouldered a senator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss Ohio' reads as a pageant title, but 'Miss' is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to leave it out, to miss it.

clue.text: Crazy Democratic fool in days long past

indicators.note: crazy means wild, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at a foolish Democrat of an earlier era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' rearranges only FOOL, giving OFOL; the abbreviation for Democratic sits at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Of old means in former times, long ago.

clue.text: Time to get behind former leader and Chief Justice

parts.note: aft means behind, at the back

explanation.surface: It is time to back a past president.
explanation.walkthrough: William Howard Taft is the only person to have been both US president and Chief Justice.
explanation.definitionFit: He served as the 27th US president and later as Chief Justice of the Supreme Court.

clue.text: Proper sign used for initial stages of public voting

parts.note: prim means primly proper
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A proper symbol is chosen to mark the early rounds of an election.
explanation.definitionFit: In US elections, preliminary votes pick each party's candidate before the general election.

clue.text: Ex-POTUS laid back early in the day with a dog he owns

indicators.note: laid back puts the pieces down backwards, so they read in reverse

parts.note: a.m. denotes the morning
Bo was the Portuguese water dog of a former US first family

explanation.surface: A relaxed former president spends the morning with his pet.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is self-referential: the dog belongs to the president who is the answer. POTUS means President of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: He served as the 44th US president, so he is a former President of the United States.

clue.text: Some get an escort around part of the Capitol Building

indicators.note: turned around means the run of letters is read backwards
only some of the letters of the words get an escort are used

explanation.surface: Visitors to the seat of US government are shown round by a guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes ETANES from 'get an escort', and 'around' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper chamber of Congress meets in its own wing of the Capitol.

clue.text: In the first instance, Biden's age is a striking characteristic

indicators.note: in the first instance points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: age here means the state of being old

explanation.surface: A commentator says a president's years are what stands out about him.
explanation.definitionFit: Boldness, being conspicuous or daring, is a quality that strikes the eye.
